title: Error whitening: Why Gauss-Newton outperforms Newton
summary: The Gauss-Newton matrix is widely viewed as a positive semidefinite approximation of the Hessian, yet mounting empirical evidence shows that Gauss-Newton descent outperforms Newton's method. We adopt a function space perspective to analyze this phenomenon. We show that the generalized Gauss-Newton (GGN) matrix projects the Newton direction in function space onto the model's tangent space, while a Jacobian-only variant obtained by applying the least squares Gauss-Newton matrix to non-least squares losses projects the function space loss gradient onto this same tangent space.
